body: Greg, 2026-11-04, relayed by Engram::Asistant: „Dl560 ma wolny single core..”, „Tak. Ale dl ma 1ghz na core, windows B ma 4ghz. Inna klasa maszyn.” and „Tak. Jest na oszczedzaniu energii ze wzgledu na hałas.” The last one is deliberate host policy: DL560 stays on power saving because of noise; don't change it or propose changing it. Asistant added: different clock speeds, architectures and loads mean no direct conclusion about a regression from timings alone between these hosts, no needless expensive comparisons, keep the host's configuration and account for it when reading NUMA and mimalloc measurements. Practical rule: compare timings only on one host, on two commits or two settings. Timings across DL560 and Windows B say nothing about product speed. Read from DL560 at 03:58Z, read only: Xeon Gold 6140, base 2.3 GHz, max 3.7 GHz, min 1.0 GHz, governor powersave with intel_pstate active, average 1160 MHz at low load and one core at 3700 MHz. 4 sockets, 4 NUMA nodes, 144 CPUs, distance 21 against 10, numa_balancing=1. A real-clock limit tuned on a fast host is harsher there, which is a test defect, not a host fault. A direct focused cargo test at the default test-thread count ran 400-620 OS threads there; a FULL at 4 threads ran 12-19. NUMA and allocator work is on w-d59057f2b3b5.
